rubriker.title: From Dusk till Dawn
rubriker._rss_content: Older readers will remember. In the old days, before the invention of the internet, you actually had to meet in person to play chess. In blitz chess, you sat opposite one another, saw each other and even talked. It was a sociable affair and, at times, rather boisterous. In Hamburg last weekend, a secret gathering of veterans took place. "From Dusk till Dawn" was the motto.

rubriker.title: "Chess might be one of the least expressive sports I have ever watched"
rubriker._rss_content: Coming from badminton and motorsport, Naganethra Reddy expected chess to feel quiet and hard to read. Watching the Global Chess League changed that: the drama was in the glances, pauses, and small gestures around the board, and in the stories shared through the commentary. Here's what she thinks. | Pictured: Bibisara Assaubayeva | Photo: Global Chess League 2026

rubriker.title: The oldest chess pieces in the world
rubriker._rss_content: In 1977, the historian and archaeologist Yuri Buryakov discovered a set of seven ivory pieces in the ruins of the ancient city of Afrasiab, near Samarkand. The pieces have been dated to the mid-seventh century and are regarded as the oldest known chess pieces in the world. | Photo: Samarkand State Museum

rubriker.title: The princes of Samarkand
rubriker._rss_content: The success of the German national team has something to do with Thuringia. The foundations were laid almost 20 years ago, when national youth coach Bernd Vökler entered a youth team as Germany's second squad at the Chess Olympiad in Dresden. The "Princes' Group" was born. Axel Eger reported for the Thüringer Allgemeine. | Photo: German Chess Federation

rubriker.title: German chess magazine SCHACH launches first English edition as CHESS INSIGHT
rubriker._rss_content: For the first time in its history, the renowned German chess magazine SCHACH is available in English. Published under the title CHESS INSIGHT, the new edition was released on October 1, 2026, and is available digitally through Forward Chess.

rubriker.title: Ilyumzhinov Says CAS Could Erase Turlov
rubriker._rss_content: Kirsan Ilyumzhinov, who ran FIDE for 23 years until 2018, says the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) could still throw out Timur Turlov's election as FIDE president.

rubriker.title: Pensamiento crítico vs. pensamiento ajedrecístico: coincidencias, diferencias y confusiones
rubriker._rss_content: El pensamiento crítico y el pensamiento ajedrecístico comparten operaciones como analizar, comparar alternativas, anticipar consecuencias y revisar errores, pero no son capacidades equivalentes. El texto examina sus coincidencias y diferencias desde la psicología cognitiva, subrayando que la pericia adquirida sobre el tablero no se transfiere automáticamente a otros ámbitos. El potencial educativo del ajedrez aparece cuando existe una mediación pedagógica capaz de conectar explícitamente ambos modos de razonamiento. | Imagen (IA): Uvencio Blanco

rubriker.title: La FIDE premia el juego limpio de Sebastian Poltorak y Tin Jingyao
rubriker._rss_content: El polaco Sebastian Poltorak y el gran maestro singapurense Tin Jingyao (en la foto) han sido reconocidos con el Trofeo Svetozar Gligoric 2026. Poltorak fue distinguido por aceptar tablas después de que su rival se encontrara indispuesto durante la Copa de Europa de Clubes, mientras que Tin renunció a reclamar una victoria por incomparecencia cuando su oponente llegó tarde debido al tráfico. La comisión designada señaló que ambos casos reflejaron un comportamiento ejemplar de juego limpio y respeto por los rivales, por encima de una ventaja competitiva inmediata. | Foto: FIDE
